title: The Impact of Climate Anxiety, Resilience, and Psychopathology on Adolescents' Time Perspectives
summary:
The influences of climate anxiety, resilience and mental illness on the time perspective are examined. Various questionnaires are to be answered for this purpose. With the questions we want to assess the fear of the consequences of global warming and at the same time investigate possible protective factors against such fears (resilience). In addition, we want to assess the severity of symptoms of various mental illnesses (ADHD, depression, anxiety disorders, traumatization and emotional instability). Both the climate fear, the protective factors and mental illness can influence the so-called time perspective. Time perspective refers to our attitudes toward the past, present, and future.
At least 800 outpatients and day-patients with mental illnesses between the ages of 14 and 20 should take part in the study.
The results of this study should give us information about risk factors for mental illnesses in childhood and adolescence. We also hope to gain insights into how we can further improve our therapies. For this reason, the survey should be carried out twice, namely at the beginning of the treatment and at the end of the treatment. This allows us to examine how treatment affects symptomatology, protective factors and time perspective.

interventions.name: Norm sample: Students between the ages of 14 and 20 complete digital questionnaires on climate anxiety, resilience and time perspectives.

Clinical sample: Patients in outpatient and day-patient child and adolescent psychiatric treatment complete digital questionnaires on climate anxiety, resilience, time perspectives and psychopathology (borderline symptoms, ADHD, depression, anxiety, PTSD symptoms).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Average intelligence according to clinical impression
Exclusion criteria:
• Intellectual disability
• Psychotic symptoms
• Illiteracy
